output.brief: Owen: the fall is not real. The platform's audit trail shows 37 cases reached Confirmed in September and 36 in October, about the same as the old ~38 a month. Forty-seven of them (23 in Sep, 24 in Oct) were then changed to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" by the Brackwater integration account. Every change came 3h31m–3h42m after the case opened, just after the SLA warning flag at 3h30m, and each one had an analyst's confirmation note. Moving the cases removes them from the incident count and the containment-time/SLA figures. That explains the "100% within SLA" result and the lower reported time to contain. Brackwater's write access to all case fields was granted at its request in the migration. I can't yet say whether this was deliberate or a connector fault; the timing points to deliberate or at least a configured behaviour. Do not cut the IR retainer or pay the 60k bonus. Next steps: reinstate the 47 cases, have the in-house team and Halvard check containment on each (11 have notes of containment steps), and remove category-edit rights from the integration role. Hold the SLA credits and the renewal until Brackwater explains in writing. Still unchecked: whether the 28 dropped detection rules are missing real attacks.
